messages:
Maria Chen: quick sync — after yesterday's outage we need to lock down the PRD changes + runbook edits before we cut the next release. outline below and can we triage scope?
Alex Rivera: +1. do we have a minimal acceptance criteria list to surface to eng?
Maria Chen: draft: 1) automatic fallback to v-small when tail latency > 1s for > 30s; 2) prefix KV cache warmup on rollout; 3) circuit-breaker metric with 5xx rate threshold; 4) canary policy must detect token-rate regressions within 5k requests.
Ben Cho: for the circuit breaker, propose: open if 5xx > 2% for 60s AND p99 latency > 2s. That avoids noisy flips.
Rachael Patel: ops note — need explicit telemetry events for each fallback so the Console can attribute cost and quality to those flows. Add event keys: fallback.reason, fallback.model, fallback.count.
Samir Gupta: customer asks: some larger customers want opt-out of fallback, prefer queued requests instead. That affects scope: opt-out requires tenant-level config + extra testing.
Maria Chen: agree. proposal: make opt-out an enterprise flag with manual approval and additional SLA caveats. keep default behavior global.
Alex Rivera: implementation risk: KV warmup will add complexity to rollout code. I can prototype warmup hook but need to push quantization checks later.
Ben Cho: runbook additions: playbook step when fallback triggers: 1) check recent deploys; 2) check routing policy changes; 3) escalate to infra on-call if fallback persists > 15m.
incident-bot: Incident #742 tagged: cache-throttle -> triggered fallback to v-small at 2026-03-20T15:12:10Z
Rachael Patel: add explicit rollback criteria to the PRD: if canary shows >3% regression in end-to-end quality for 10k eval calls, auto-rollback. Also require manual sign-off for any rollback during peak hours.
Maria Chen: acceptance checklist (short): - unit tests for fallback decision logic; - e2e smoke that validates fallback telemetry; - runbook step & playbook tested in staging; - docs: customer opt-out and SLA note.
Samir Gupta: prioritization: customers asking for opt-out + SLA language are paying signals — maybe elevate enterprise flag to P1 for Dedicated+Private customers. Keep global fallback improvements P2 for Hosted. Thoughts?
Alex Rivera: that seems reasonable. P1 for opt-out + KMS/SLA legal wording; P2 for warmup and canary sensitivity tuning. P3 for niceties (dashboarding extras).
Ben Cho: edge cases: what if fallback cycles between models rapidly? add cooldown: once fallback engages, lock routing for 2 minutes and ramp back with exponential backoff.
Maria Chen: good. I'll add that to PRD "fallback_lock_minutes": "2" and backoff policy. Also add acceptance criteria to prove cooldown doesn't hide a systemic failure (tests that simulate continuous 5xx).
Rachael Patel: need to update runbook section "During fallback" with explicit commands and logs to check, e.g.:
```
# check canary metrics
curl -s "https://console.internal/api/v1/metrics?query=canary_fault_rate" | jq .
# inspect last deploy
git log -1 --pretty=oneline
```
Samir Gupta: client impact note — docs must warn that opting out may cause request queuing and increased customer-visible latency; legal should approve SLA language.
Maria Chen: next steps / owners: Alex - prototype warmup hook (ETA 1 sprint), Ben - update runbook + cooldown logic (ETA 3 days), Rachael - telemetry events + docs (ETA 2 days), Samir - coordinate enterprise opt-out + legal (ETA 1 week). I'll update PRD and send for review by EOD.
Alex Rivera: ack. I'll PR a design doc for the warmup hook and include perf regression tests.
Ben Cho: I'll add the new playbook steps to eng-oncall channel and run a dry-run in staging tomorrow at 09:30.
Rachael Patel: will mock the telemetry events in staging and verify Console shows fallback counts by tenant.
Maria Chen: thanks — if nothing else, I'll consolidate and post a PRD diff. tagging @here for visibility. :white_check_mark:
Samir Gupta: thanks all.
Maria Chen: (follow-up) I pushed a small PRD diff to the docs repo, link posted in #docs later.
